narrative: Interstate 40 at Washington closed for east bound and west bound traffic.
Water was flowing over a low spot on Faceville Attapulgus Road.
Flag Mine Road was closed due to flooding.
Flooding was reported at 500 Old Mill Road.
Heavy rain of 1 to 1.5 fell in less that 1 hour in the Catalina Foothills. Ventana Wash rose and flowed up to 18 deep across Snyder Rd, causing its closure.
A webcam showed the Vock Wash flooded Stockton Hill Rd.
Runoff due to heavy rain from thunderstorms caused an un-named creek to overflow its banks and cause flooding across Elkin Highway in North Wilkesboro.
A trained spotter reported part of Missionary Ridge Road near Bon Aqua was washed out due to flooding.
TSpotter Twitter reports indicated McEwen Drive at Carothers Parkway in Franklin was flooded and impassable.
Pump Station Road was closed due to flooding.
Water was reported over Highway 256 near Wrights Chapel Road due to a long duration of moderate to heavy rainfall.
Public reported on social media that there was flash flooding on Main Street in San Angelo.
DW Ranch Road was closed due to flooding.
A portion of Scottwood Dr was washed out due to flash flooding.

Numerous homes and business sustained severe flood damage across the county. Numerous roads were severely damaged or washed away across the county. Table Rock State Park suffered flood damage according to park officials. This report will contain the total dollar estimate for flood damage to infrastructure, businesses, and homes across Taney County.
Apache Road was closed due to flooding of the McKenzie Wash.
Santa Fe Pike is flooded and impassable.
Route H was closed at Ingalls Creek due to flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Parr Wade Road was flooded due to high flow through Pettit Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred, falling on already wet soils, resulting in flash flooding.
Public video of flooding at least two feet deep with scattered debris and water damage near 50th Street and Armstrong Street.
WFAA media reported a closed highway/ramp due to high water at I-35E and Market Center.
A NWS employee reported the low water crossing over Galloway Creek on Girdley Street in West Plains was flooded.
Heavy rain was causing flooding of roads and low lying areas in parts of Plano. One impacted area was highway ramps and low lying roads at the US 75 and President George Bush Turnpike exchange.
Flash flooding caused Twin Peaks Road at Sanders Road to be closed.
Kirk Trail Rd in Holladay was closed due to washout conditions from heavy rain.
Old Nogales Highway at Summit Street closed due to flash flooding.
The intersection of Moore's Lane and Summerhill Road was flooded and closed.
Esquire Peek Road partially washed out from heavy rains.  Approximately 2 to 3 inches fell in less than an hour.
Leatherwood Road near Highway 50 was flooded.
A portion of Seaboard Street was washed out due to flood waters. Flood waters impacted a few nearby structures.
The 3500 block of South Street in Nacogdoches was flooded and closed. A water rescue was needed for a stalled vehicle in the flood waters.
Excessive rainfall caused flash flooding on County Road 441. A small tributary of Brown Branch washed out a section of County Road 441 making it impassable.

The Emergency Manager reported water rescues due to flash flooding in the 2200 block of Verbana Street. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported the closure of Country Club Road due to flooding of a nearby pond. In addition to the 1.5 inches of rain that fell the previous day, radar estimates indicate that an additional 6 to 8 inches fell on March 26, resulting in the flash flooding.
The low water crossing on Highway Y at Cowskin Creek was flooded and impassable.

Flooding from Dutch Creek flooded the property of Valle Crucis Elementary School all the way up to the school building. Water did enter portions of the building, but cleanup was quick and no damage was reported in the building.  Cleanup of the school grounds consisted mainly of debris removal.

U.S. Highway 221 Business was closed due to flooding caused by heavy rain from a thunderstorm.  Rainfall rates from the storm were observed to be three to four inches per hour, with a total of around 1.5 inches.
U.S. Highway 84 was reported to be underwater and shut down at Lazy Lou Crossing. Traffic was diverted to another route.
Sixteenth St and Avenue B in Yuma closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.
Significant flooding at Macon Road and Jackson Avenue. Several cars were stalled in 2-3 feet of water.
Sammons Road and Harpers Chapel Road were washed out due to flash flooding.
A portion of Elkton Road was washed out and closed due to flood waters.
Oatman Highway was damaged by flooding of the Warm Springs Wash.
Water was reported over the roadway on Pineknot Road.
Little Swamp Creek caused flooding of nearby roads.
The 1900 block of Moultrie Road was flooded and closed due to a long duration of moderate to heavy rainfall.

Heavy rain across Montgomery County caused flooding in the Woodstock Estates subdivision, located off Trenton Road. Approximately fourteen homes in the subdivision were inundated with six to eight feet of water. Emergency responders had to assist in evacuating several of the residents. Damages are a rough estimate.

Heavy rain caused Little Buffalo Creek to overflow its banks several inches deep across South Main  Street in the Town of West Jefferson.  No damage was reported to the road, which was open to traffic after the water receded.
Water was flowing across Masonboro Sound Rd. at Finian Dr.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that caused flash flooding resulting in cars being trapped in high water at Toll 130 and Hwy 71 near Onion Creek.
State Route BB was closed at Crane Creek due to flooding.

Carroll County Emergency Management reported rising water from a creek entered homes on Carroll Circle. Radar estimates indicate rainfall amounts of 2 to 2.5 inches, with locally higher amounts, occurred over a short period of time.
Flooding was reported near 112 Bessel Church Road.
State Highway 43 was closed due to flooding from Frazier Creek.
There was water over the road on Highway 65 near mile mark 65.
State Highway 142 was flooded and closed.
County Road V was closed due to flooding of Weaubleau Creek.
Highway BB was closed due to flooding at the Dry Auglaize Creek low water crossing.
Richland Creek crested at 9.66 feet in moderate flood stage, which is the 3rd highest stage on record for this river gauge.
Nearby Moccasin Creek flooded Holt Pond Road.

Wilson County Emergency Management reported flash flooding in and around Lebanon. A water rescue of a person swept away was conducted off South Cumberland Street near Spring Street where both roads were submerged by rushing water. Bethany Lane east of Lebanon, and a nearby bridge on Trousdale Ferry Road, were also submerged by rushing water and closed.
Several homes and businesses were flooded near Highway 70 South across from Tristart Horizon Hospital.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in the eastern part of Memphis. The left lane of I-240 at the I-40 interchange was covered with a foot of water. The ramp to I-40 eastbound from Sycamore View Road was also flooded.
NCDOT cameras showed flooding at the intersection of Albacore Street and Ocean Trail (North Carolina Highway 12).

The Emergency Manager reported the closures of South New Salem Road and West McIntosh Road likely due to flooding of the roadways from Heads Creek and the Heads Creek reservoir. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 4 inches of rain fell quickly over the area, overwhelming the small creeks and drainage systems.

Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. The San Antonio Fire Department made a water rescue at 11700 S. Hausman Rd. near French Creek in northwestern San Antonio. Rainfall totals in the area were between two and four inches.

Radar Road was closed north of the intersection with Ararat Road due to flooding from the Ararat River. The river exceeded flood stage of 13 feet between around 800 AM EST and 1200 PM EST, cresting at 13.48 feet.

Videos showed washes overflowing in Fountain Hills, with water moving across Golden Eagle Park and then downstream over North El Pueblo Boulevard. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Highway Y along Flat Creek was closed due to flooding.

The Middle Fork South Fork of the New River at Deerfield Road crested at 6.92 feet at 11 am on the 11th and remained above 6.5 feet into late afternoon. This stream overflowed its banks across Deerfield Road.

Videos on social media showed high flow in a wash near the San Carlos Apache Indian Reservation line between Globe and San Carlos, making low water crossings through the wash impassable. Further downstream, a 5 ft rise was recorded in Gilson Wash. No damage or injuries were reported.
A small area on Fair Street was briefly evacuated as a precaution along Flat Creek.
Darlington Avenue was closed due to flooding between Broad Street and Frog Pond Place due to a retention pond overflowing.
South Reilly Road between Willowbrook Drive and Lexi Lane was closed due to flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported that a majority of the Peachtree Battle Area - Atlanta Memorial Park along Peachtree Creek is underwater due to heavy rain and flooding of the creek. The nearby USGS river gage on Peachtree Creek (AANG1) crest at 19.06 feet in Moderate Flood Stage. Radar estimates indicate that 4 to 5 inches of rain occurred over the area, causing the flash flooding.
Farm Road 174 for about 1 mile west of Highway ZZ was completely flooded with several culverts washed out.
Several roads along Chat Creek were closed with flowing water.
Tatum Road between Highway 100 and Highway 7 was closed and impassable due to flooding.

USGS stream gage on Pinal Creek at Inspiration Dam measured a rapid rise from 1.28 feet at 1745 MST to 5.20 feet at 1800 MST. A radar estimated 2 to 3 inches of rain fell over the area, including a portion of the 2020 Salt burn scar, between 1610 MST and 1730 MST. Additional smaller rises were measured at 2000 MST and 2330 MST that may have been related to a different flood wave that moved through the Globe area around 1800-1900 MST. No damages or injuries were reported.
Emergency management reported a high water rescue near the intersection of FM 4 and Lakeview Dr.
Several cars were stalled in flood waters and needed water rescues along Wake Forest Rd.
State Route 198 closed in both directions between Hillcrest Circle Drive and Paul Coffman Drive due to flooding.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding north of Uvalde. The Uvalde Fire Department rescued a person from high water on Puccini Ln along the Taylor Slough in Uvalde.

The Emergency Manager reported Flooding along the Old Tennessee Highway due to high water on Pettit Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain have occurred, falling on already wet soils, resulting in flash flooding.
A vehicle was trapped in flood waters near the intersection of Grand Summit Apartment Ln and Friendway Rd.
Cooper Police reported high water over the roadway on Texas State Highway 24. Highway 24 was closed near Cooper due to the high water.

The Emergency Manager reported high water near Collard Valley Road and Fish Creek Road that submerged vehicles. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 3 inches of rain occurred over the area, causing the flash flooding.

Heavy rain fell across Gaines County and produced flash flooding on Highway 385 between Seminole and Seagraves.  The flooding was reported on Highway 385 between County Roads 103 and 124.  Other reports were received that indicate numerous county roads northwest of Seminole were flooded and impassable.  Seminole and Seagraves fire departments were pulling cars out of ditches.  The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Hackberry Road was closed from Highway 93 to Austin Peak Road.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. ATXFloods reported the low water crossing at the Woodview Mobile Home Park on West Bouldin Creek off Oltorf St. was closed in Austin.
Belle Meade Blvd and the Belle Meade Plaza parking garage on Harding Road were flooded.
The intersection of Highway 83 and FM 1407 and also Loop 517 were reportedly flooded.
The low water crossing at Route BB was closed due to flooding at Cahoochie Creek just south of the Hickory County line.
High water was reported across Clax Branch Road with a vehicle reportedly washed into Caney Branch. No injuries.
Route Z along Elk Creek was flooded and impassable.

The Emergency Manager reported water over the roadway at the intersection of South Warren Street and Underwood Road, and Vinson Highway and South Wayne Street. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 3 inches of rain occurred, falling on already wet soils and resulting in flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported the road washed out at Pebble Creek Road and Jeff Davis Road. In addition to the 1 inch of rain that fell the previous day, radar estimates indicate that 6 to 8 inches fell on March 26, resulting in the flash flooding.
Highway AB was closed just east of Highway 5 due to flooding.

Water rescue reported near Paint Your Wagon Trail and 14th St in Phoenix due to excessive runoff from Desert Hills Wash. A man was trapped inside a pickup truck with water levels almost reaching the windows. No injuries reported.

Low water crossing along Matlock Drive was overcome by the flood waters of Pinal Creek. Jesse Hayes Road nearby was also overcome by the floodwaters of both Pinal Creek and Hayes Gulch. No damages or injuries reported.
